changes.current_line: Every payout reconciles automatically to its transactions and your ERP.
changes.change: For finance buyers (CFO, controller) at regional B2B and distribution companies, open the first call with this line instead of M1: "Know where every deposit came from: each one matched to its transactions and to the invoice in your ERP, without the month-end archaeology." Use "deposits" rather than "payouts" with finance audiences. Do not claim it fixes the whole close.
changes.why: Reconciliation was the only part of the demo that got a reaction, and the CFO stopped the demo to go back to it (E25, E26). She talked about "the deposits" and wanting to know "where my money is," not about payouts (E42, E43, E7), and manual matching was only part of a nine-day close (E6).

changes.current_line: Proven ROI, backed by an independent economic impact study.
changes.change: For finance buyers: "Send us one month of your statements and we'll show you your own cost of manual matching: your number, not ours." Offer the one-month statement teardown as a standard step early in the sale, not as a late rescue.
changes.why: The deal went from "dead" at 20 percent to paperwork after a single working session on one month of the customer's own statements (E35, E28, E34). The CFO valued that it was "my number, not yours" (E32), which works against leading with an independent study.

changes.current_line: Financial infrastructure to grow globally, in every currency.
changes.change: Stop opening first calls with M1 for regional, single-country B2B and distribution buyers. Move it and the M2 developer story to an appendix or a later IT conversation, and lead with the reconciliation line (M9) instead.
changes.why: The standard "financial infrastructure, global growth, all the currencies" opener got silence (E21). This buyer's four-person IT team "aren't building anything" (E24), and "nobody said 'infrastructure'" during the deal (E43).

changes.current_line: Support plans with tiered response times, up to 24/7 coverage.
changes.change: Against bank-bundled incumbents, lead support messaging with "A named contact who knows your account, not a bank rep who changes without telling you," with tiered response times as the supporting detail. Use this only where the plan actually includes a named contact. When the incumbent offers "we can look at your rates," answer with visibility ("we show you where your money is") plus the named contact, not a discount.
changes.why: After talking to her bank, the CFO's one new question was whether she would get a named contact (E19), because her bank rep had changed and she didn't know the new one (E20). The incumbent's rate-review offer missed her actual concern (E16, E17).
